newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Monsanto backs '97 mean view.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Monsanto backs '97 mean view.

text.p: Monsanto Co, which posted first-quarter earnings that were above analysts' expectations, said Tuesday it backs the current First Call mean estimate for full-year 1997 earnings of $1.69 a share.
"I'm not uncomfortable with the mean at this point," Nicholas Filippello, Monsanto's chief economist, said.

He cautioned that while Monsanto's first quarter earnings of $0.56 a share before charges beat the consensus of $0.51, some agricultural sales and earnings may have been pulled forward into the first quarter from the second quarter.
In the first quarter, Monsanto took a $101 million pretax write-off of acquired in-process research and development related to its acquistion of Asgrow Agronomics and a small seed company in Brazil.

Filippello said Monsanto expects to take further research write-offs later in the year related to pending acquisitions, which include Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc, Corn States Hybrid Service Inc and Corn States International.
He did not specify how large the write-off would be, but added it would "probably be some multiple of what we took in the first quarter."
Filippello said he expects Monsanto's agricultural operations to have another strong year, benefiting from increased sales of its Roundup herbicide as well as biotechnology crops.
He added increased acreage is expected for the biotech crops such as soybeans, cotton and canola that are resistant to Roundup, as well as insect-resistant Bt cotton, Bt corn and Bt potatoes.
Higher G.D. Searle pharmaceutical sales in the first quarter benefited from increased demand for the Ambien insomnia drug.
Ambien captured 47.9 percent of new prescriptions written in the first quarter, compared with 40.2 percent a year ago.
Chemical operations in the first quarter benefited from strong sales volumes for its Saflex plastic interlayer used in laminated glass, particularly in Europe.

Filippello said pricing was mixed with nylon prices in the first quarter flat compared with the fourth quarter of 1996 but up slightly compared with a year ago. Saflex pricing was down a little compared with a year ago, but up from the 1996 fourth quarter, he added.
The spin off of the chemical operations, which was previously announced, is expected to take place in the third quarter after special shareholder approval.
